answer: To resist sybil attacks, the agent economy can require each identity to craft a unique computational sonnet: a short proof poem that whispers a private nonce derived from the epoch seed and echoes a peer's prior attestation hash. Generating this sonnet demands non-reusable local computation that scales with the number of identities an attacker controls, so faking many accounts costs proportionally more resources than honest single-agent participation. Peers then verify the echo consistency on-ledger before accepting the identity for mining.
